caption: The Uber Eats number nearly broke me and I only just started earning properly. What's yours?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R17 500
p/m salary
Living in Pretoria
slides.body:
Male, 24
Single, renting a room
Job: IT support technician
Net salary: R17 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Backyard room in Sunnyside, water and wifi included
slides.body: It's one room and a kettle. It's also ten minutes from work, which is the only reason I can afford to be here.

slides.title: Transport (Uber & taxi)
slides.includes: Uber to work most days, taxi when the app surges
slides.body: No car yet. Some months this line costs more than a car instalment would.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers, and the Pick n Pay top-ups when I run out mid-month
slides.body: I cook for one and still buy too much bread.

slides.title: Personal loan
slides.includes: R19 500 taken out for a laptop and a phone, both needed for the job
slides.body: Sixteen months left. I needed both just to start earning this salary.

slides.title: Takeaways & delivery
slides.includes: Uber Eats after late shifts, weekend takeaways
slides.body: I guessed R700. I checked. It was R2 000. Ordering in feels smaller each time than it is in total.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Airtime & data, electricity, funeral policy, stokvel, clothing account, black tax, savings
slides.body: Seven small debit orders I've never added up in one sitting. Together they're almost a third of what I earn.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R17 500. That's about R25 a day until payday, and I've only been earning like this for four months.

slides.title: I stopped guessing where it went
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The Uber Eats and delivery apps alone came to R2 000 — I would have guessed R700.

No bank login needed.
